requirements.risks: Account deletion is a privacy expectation and, in several jurisdictions, a legal one for a consumer app that stores personal data. Leaving an orphaned pantry subcollection behind after deletion would be a data-retention problem.
requirements.caveats: Scope depends on whether FridgeFit is intended to ship publicly, which the inaccessible Notion specification would clarify.

requirements.name: App settings and preferences
requirements.description: The user can configure app behaviour — preferred units, appearance, notifications, or an Apple Intelligence status indicator.
requirements.evidence: No implementation found. No settings screen, no UserDefaults usage and no preference model anywhere in the codebase.
requirements.missing: Settings UI and a preference store.
requirements.remaining: Decide which settings matter. A visible Apple Intelligence availability indicator would be genuinely useful here: AppleIntelligenceAvailability already produces user-facing titles and explanations, but they are only ever shown inside a feature the user has already tried and found unavailable.
requirements.risks: None.
requirements.caveats: Not confirmed as a requirement. The availability-indicator idea is a recommendation, not a verified missing requirement.

requirements.name: Automated unit test suite
requirements.description: Domain logic, use cases, parsers, validators and view models are covered by an automated test suite that runs locally.
requirements.evidence: A FridgeFitTests target holds 23 XCTest classes with 240 test methods, organised to mirror the production tree (Data, Domain, UseCases, ViewModels, Support). Coverage is concentrated where the risk is: 25 cases on the normaliser, 19 on the line parser, 18 on the canonicaliser, 18 on the scanner view model, 16 on feasibility, 15 on pantry suggestions, 14 each on the quantity parser and the substitution validator. Shared fixtures live in Support/SampleReceipt.swift and Support/TestImage.swift. Every external dependency has a double — InMemoryPantryRepository, InMemoryRecipeRepository, MockReceiptTextRecognizer, MockReceiptIngredientInterpreter, MockRecipeSuggestionService, MockSubstitutionService — plus a StubURLProtocol for the HTTP client, so the whole suite runs with no network, no camera, no device and no live credentials.
requirements.missing: Nothing for this requirement. Coverage gaps in specific areas are recorded against the requirements they belong to (CD-AUTH-09, CD-SCAN-02, CD-INFRA-05).
requirements.remaining: None for the suite's existence.
requirements.risks: No code-coverage measurement was produced, so 240 tests is a count of cases rather than a measure of lines reached. The doubles live in the production target rather than the test target, which keeps them available to SwiftUI previews but also ships mock code in the app binary.
requirements.caveats: The suite was executed in this audit; see the testExecution block for the result. The tests are unusually behavioural — many assert documented invariants by name, including the adversarial cases where a model contradicts the pantry.

requirements.name: Layered architecture with testable boundaries
requirements.description: The app separates presentation, presentation state, domain logic and data access, with every external dependency behind a protocol.
requirements.evidence: The separation holds throughout and is not merely nominal. Views contain no business logic (AddPantryItemView's comment — 'Just collects input' — is accurate: validation is in the use case). View models map results and own no rules (PantryViewModel delegates every decision; RecipeViewModel never computes feasibility). All twelve use cases are plain value types taking protocol dependencies by injection. Six protocols isolate every external system, and each has both a production adapter and a double. The one consistent exception is AuthViewModel, which calls the Auth.auth() singleton directly and is consequently the only untestable view model — the exception that demonstrates the rule.
tests: Demonstrated by the suite: every use case and four of five view models are tested with doubles
requirements.missing: Nothing for this requirement.
requirements.remaining: Bring AuthViewModel behind a protocol so it matches the rest of the codebase (tracked as CD-AUTH-09).
requirements.risks: All dependency wiring happens in ContentView.init, which is 38 lines of construction. It works and is readable, but it couples the root view to every concrete type in the app and is the reason view models are not rebuilt on an account change (CD-AUTH-04).
requirements.caveats: The trust boundary is the strongest architectural property here: every generative-model output enters as an untrusted Raw* value and must pass a deterministic validator before any view sees it. That pattern is applied consistently across all three AI features.

requirements.name: Secrets excluded from version control
requirements.description: API keys and Firebase configuration are never committed to the repository.
requirements.evidence: .gitignore excludes GoogleService-Info.plist and Secrets.xcconfig. Config.xcconfig is committed but contains no credential: it optionally includes Secrets.xcconfig with #include? so a fresh checkout still builds when the file is absent, and sets only a non-secret model identifier. Secrets.example.xcconfig documents the required key with a placeholder value and a link to obtain one. Info.plist references $(OPENROUTER_API_KEY) as a build-setting substitution rather than a literal. OpenRouterConfiguration.loadFromInfoPlist returns nil on an empty key so callers fall back to an explicit error rather than sending an empty credential. git ls-files confirms neither GoogleService-Info.plist nor Secrets.xcconfig is tracked.
requirements.missing: Nothing for this requirement.
requirements.remaining: None.
requirements.risks: The same arrangement is why substitutions are non-functional in a fresh clone (CD-SUBST-01) and why the app cannot authenticate without the Firebase config being supplied separately. Both are correct trade-offs that need to be stated in setup documentation — of which there is none, as the repository has no README.
requirements.caveats: This audit deliberately did not read or report any credential value. Config.xcconfig was inspected with values redacted, and Secrets.xcconfig does not exist in the working tree.

requirements.name: Firestore rules and indexes under version control and deployed
requirements.description: Backend configuration is versioned alongside the app and matches what the live project enforces.
requirements.evidence: firebase.json, firestore.rules and firestore.indexes.json are all tracked in git. The rules were added deliberately in commit 172a3b0 ('chore(firestore): add security rules scoping pantry to the signed-in user'). firestore.indexes.json is empty, which is consistent with the only query being a single-field order(by: "ingredientName") that Firestore indexes automatically.
requirements.missing: No evidence of deployment. Having the rules in the repository is not the same as the live project enforcing them. See CD-PANTRY-07.
requirements.remaining: Deploy and record it; add rules unit tests.
requirements.risks: See CD-PANTRY-07 — the security consequence if the live project is still on test-mode rules.
requirements.caveats: Versioning backend configuration alongside the app is good practice and is done correctly here.

requirements.name: UI, integration and end-to-end tests
requirements.description: Automated tests exercise real user journeys through the UI and real integrations, not only units behind doubles.
requirements.evidence: No implementation found. There is no UI test target: the project defines exactly two targets, FridgeFit and FridgeFitTests, and a search for XCUIApplication across all Swift sources returns nothing. No Firebase Emulator Suite configuration or integration test exists. Every one of the 240 tests is a unit test running against doubles.
requirements.missing: A UI test target and journey tests (sign in -> add pantry item -> browse recipes -> open a recipe), plus emulator-backed integration tests for Firestore CRUD and rules.
requirements.remaining: Add a UI test target with two or three high-value journeys, and emulator tests for the four Firestore operations. These would close CD-PANTRY-06, CD-PANTRY-07 and part of CD-AUTH-09 at once.
requirements.risks: This is the structural reason so much of this audit reads needs_verification. Excellent unit coverage proves each part behaves correctly in isolation; nothing proves the parts work together against real services. The scan-to-Firestore path (CD-SCAN-10) is the clearest casualty.
requirements.caveats: Some of this cannot be automated — the Apple Intelligence paths need real hardware — but Firestore and authentication are both automatable today with the emulator suite.

requirements.name: Continuous integration
requirements.description: The test suite runs automatically on every push or pull request.
requirements.evidence: No implementation found. The repository has no .github directory and no CI configuration of any kind (no Xcode Cloud workflow, Fastlane, Bitrise or similar). git history shows the feature-branch-and-merge discipline a CI pipeline would normally gate — six feature branches merged into main — but nothing ran automatically.
requirements.missing: A workflow that builds and tests on a macOS runner.
requirements.remaining: Add a GitHub Actions workflow running xcodebuild test on an iOS 26.1 simulator. Two prerequisites first: commit a shared Xcode scheme (CD-INFRA-07), and handle the gitignored GoogleService-Info.plist and Secrets.xcconfig, since the app target will not build without the former.
requirements.risks: With 240 tests and no automation, a regression is caught only when someone remembers to run the suite locally.
requirements.caveats: The secrets arrangement that is correct for a public repository (CD-INFRA-03) is exactly what makes CI setup non-trivial — the runner needs the Firebase config injected from a secret.

requirements.name: Shared Xcode scheme for reproducible builds
requirements.description: The build and test configuration is committed so any machine or CI runner builds the project identically.
requirements.evidence: No shared scheme is committed. A search for *.xcscheme under FridgeFit.xcodeproj returns nothing; the only scheme data is xcuserdata/kai.xcuserdatad/xcschemes/xcschememanagement.plist, and xcuserdata/ is gitignored. The scheme used by this audit's test run was autocreated by Xcode. Separately, the working tree has an uncommitted change adding DEVELOPMENT_TEAM to both build configurations in project.pbxproj — a machine-specific signing identity sitting in a shared file.
requirements.missing: A shared FridgeFit.xcscheme under xcshareddata/xcschemes/, with the test target's membership recorded explicitly.
requirements.remaining: Mark the scheme Shared in Xcode and commit it. Decide whether the uncommitted DEVELOPMENT_TEAM change belongs in version control; a developer-specific team id in a shared pbxproj breaks other developers' builds.
requirements.risks: Without a shared scheme, xcodebuild on another machine relies on autocreation, which may not include the test target. This is a prerequisite for CI.
requirements.caveats: Autocreation worked on this machine, so the gap is reproducibility elsewhere rather than a broken build here.

requirements.name: Accessibility support
requirements.description: The app is usable with VoiceOver and respects the system's accessibility settings.
requirements.evidence: Accessibility is addressed deliberately rather than incidentally. Pantry rows are accessibilityElement(children: .combine) with a composed label naming the item, category and quantity, plus a hint ('Double tap to update quantity'). Form fields carry explicit accessibilityLabels. Receipt review rows label the tick with its state and a hint naming the item, and the quantity field's label changes to say when the receipt stated no amount. The scanning indicator is combined and labelled. Decorative IconBadges are accessibilityHidden. Standard SwiftUI components (List, Form, Picker, ContentUnavailableView) are used throughout, which brings Dynamic Type and VoiceOver support by default.
requirements.missing: No accessibility audit was run and no VoiceOver or Dynamic Type verification exists. Colour is used to carry feasibility and availability meaning (green/orange/red/blue), always paired with an SF Symbol and a text label, which is the right mitigation but is unverified for contrast. Nothing checks behaviour at the largest accessibility text sizes, where the receipt review row's fixed 110-point quantity field and three side-by-side controls are the most likely to break.
requirements.remaining: Run Xcode's Accessibility Inspector audit on each screen, test with VoiceOver, and check the largest Dynamic Type sizes — particularly ReceiptItemReviewView.
requirements.risks: The receipt review row packs a text field and two pickers into one horizontal stack with a fixed-width frame; at large text sizes this is likely to clip or overflow.
requirements.caveats: This is better accessibility work than most projects of this size contain. It is marked partial for lack of verification, not lack of effort.

requirements.name: Localization
requirements.description: User-facing text is localisable rather than hardcoded.
requirements.evidence: No implementation found. No .lproj directories, no Localizable.strings and no String Catalog (.xcstrings) exist. Every user-facing string is an inline English literal, including all seven LocalizedError types' errorDescription values. Some locale awareness is present where it matters most — ListFormatter.localizedString for the scan summary, and Vision recognition languages preferring en-AU — but the strings themselves are fixed.
requirements.missing: A String Catalog and extraction of all literals.
requirements.remaining: Add a String Catalog and migrate strings, starting with the error types since they are the most numerous and the most user-visible.
requirements.risks: Low for an English-market product. Note that the domain is Australian-specific in several places by design — the canonicaliser's dialect table, the receipt parser's metadata words, the prompt's abbreviation list — so localisation would mean more than translating strings.
requirements.caveats: Not confirmed as a requirement, and reasonable to defer.

requirements.name: Analytics and crash reporting
requirements.description: Production failures and usage are observable.
requirements.evidence: No implementation found. Only FirebaseAuth, FirebaseCore and FirebaseFirestore are linked — no Crashlytics, no Analytics, no Performance Monitoring. OSLog is used well for diagnostics in VisionReceiptTextRecognizer, AppleReceiptIngredientInterpreter and AppleRecipeSuggestionService, but those logs stay on the device.
requirements.missing: Crash reporting and any usage telemetry.
requirements.remaining: Add Crashlytics if the app is to be distributed. Analytics is a product and privacy decision, not a technical one.
requirements.risks: Without crash reporting, a device-specific failure in the Apple Intelligence paths — exactly the code this audit could not verify — would be invisible after release.
requirements.caveats: ReceiptScanDiagnostics deliberately uses print rather than Logger, behind #if DEBUG, with the reasoning documented: a receipt records what someone bought, where and when, and the unified log persists on device and is collectable in a sysdiagnose. That is a thoughtful privacy decision and any future telemetry should preserve it.

roadmap.label: Critical — blocks essential functionality or a truthful completeness claim

tasks.title: Obtain the Notion Feature List and re-run the requirement mapping
tasks.work: Export the Notion Feature List to Markdown or CSV and commit it to docs/, or configure a Notion integration token. Then re-map every Notion requirement onto this audit's CD-* records.
tasks.acceptance: Every Notion requirement has a status, evidence and remaining-work entry, and the overall completion percentage is computable and stated with its method.
tasks.effortAssumption: Assumes the export is straightforward and the list is comparable in size to this 65-item baseline. Re-mapping, not re-auditing — the code evidence is already gathered.
tasks.why: Until this is done, no statement about overall project completion can be made honestly, and any Notion requirement with zero implementation is invisible to this report by construction.

tasks.title: Deploy and test the Firestore security rules
tasks.work: Run firebase deploy --only firestore:rules against the live project. Add @firebase/rules-unit-testing cases asserting that user A cannot read or write user B's pantry and that unauthenticated access is denied.
tasks.acceptance: Rules are confirmed live in the Firebase console, and automated rules tests pass for the cross-user denial and unauthenticated-denial cases.
tasks.effortAssumption: Rules are already written and correct; this is deployment plus a small test harness.
tasks.why: If the live project is still on test-mode rules, every user's pantry is readable by any authenticated client. The client-side uid scoping is a correctness measure, not a security boundary.

tasks.title: Verify Firestore pantry CRUD against the Firebase Emulator Suite
tasks.work: Configure the emulator in firebase.json and add integration tests covering fetchAll, add, update and remove, plus the notAuthenticated path. Inject a fixed UID through the existing userIDProvider seam.
tasks.acceptance: Automated tests create, read, update and delete a pantry item against the emulator and assert the stored field shape, including both server timestamps.
tasks.effortAssumption: Assumes first-time emulator setup for this project. The injectable userIDProvider already exists, so no production change is needed.
tasks.why: Every feature's persistence runs through this repository and only its pure mapping functions are tested. fetchAll silently compactMaps away any undecodable document, which would present to a user as an item quietly vanishing.

tasks.title: Run one documented end-to-end receipt scan on capable hardware
tasks.work: On an Apple Intelligence-capable device running iOS 26.x with the feature enabled and the Firebase config in place, photograph several real grocery receipts from different retailers. Record OCR line recovery, how often the model echoes originalText exactly enough to be matched, classification accuracy on ambiguous items such as milk and stock, and confirm the resulting documents in the Firebase console. Repeat for Pantry Ideas.
tasks.acceptance: A written record exists of at least three real receipts scanned end to end, with per-stage observations and the Firestore documents verified. The rowGroupingTolerance and minimumLineConfidence values are either validated or adjusted against that evidence.
dependencies: iPhone 15 Pro or later (or M-series iPad) with Apple Intelligence enabled and model assets downloaded
tasks.effortAssumption: Assumes a capable device is available. Mostly measurement and note-taking rather than coding, unless the evidence shows the tuning constants need changing.
tasks.why: This is the project's headline feature and its single largest unverified claim. The 240 green unit tests prove each stage is correct against doubles; none of them touch real OCR, a real model, or a real database.

tasks.title: Fix the stale camera usage description
tasks.work: Rewrite NSCameraUsageDescription to describe photographing a grocery receipt, and update CameraAccess.denied's explanation and CameraPicker's doc comment to match.
tasks.acceptance: Both user-visible strings describe receipt photography; no reference to photographing a fridge remains.
tasks.why: A purpose string that does not match actual camera use is a recognised App Store review rejection reason, and it misleads the user at the moment they decide whether to grant access. Cheapest high-value fix in this report.

tasks.title: Configure OpenRouter credentials and validate substitutions live
tasks.work: Create Secrets.xcconfig from Secrets.example.xcconfig with a valid key. Make a handful of real requests and record latency, JSON-schema compliance and whether the model attempts to assert pantry availability despite the prompt forbidding it. Confirm the hardcoded default model identifier is still available.
tasks.acceptance: Find Substitute returns validated suggestions on a real recipe, and the observed behaviour is recorded. The default model string is confirmed live or updated.
tasks.effortAssumption: Configuration plus observation. No code change expected unless the default model has been withdrawn.
tasks.why: A demonstration from a fresh clone currently shows this feature failing with 'Substitution suggestions aren't set up yet'. The failure is graceful and names the fix, but the feature is non-functional until a key exists.

tasks.title: Build the dietary preferences profile
tasks.work: Add a dietary preferences model, persist it per user in Firestore with matching security rules, add the Profile editing UI, and pass the values from SubstitutionViewModel into GetIngredientSubstitutionsUseCase.
tasks.acceptance: A saved restriction survives relaunch, appears in the substitution prompt, and a conflicting suggestion is filtered out before reaching the UI. Any user-facing wording avoids implying allergen-grade protection.
dependencies: P0 task 2 (rules) so the new collection is covered
tasks.effortAssumption: Assumes a simple tag list rather than a structured allergen taxonomy. The enforcement mechanism already exists and is tested, so the work is the profile and the wiring.
tasks.why: This single absence makes CD-SUBST-05 inert: the enforcement path is built and tested but the list is always empty, so a user with a nut allergy has no way to tell FridgeFit and the feature will suggest peanut butter. Note that the existing keyword check is explicitly not an allergen database.

tasks.title: Make authentication testable and test it
tasks.work: Introduce an auth-service protocol so AuthViewModel stops calling the Auth.auth() singleton directly, then test sign-in success, failure messaging, sign-up, sign-out and the loading flag. Explicitly test the account-switch scenario: sign out, sign in as a different user, confirm the Pantry tab shows the second user's data and the SubstitutionCache does not serve stale entries.
tasks.acceptance: AuthViewModel is covered by unit tests behind a double, and the account-switch scenario is verified.
tasks.effortAssumption: Small production refactor plus tests. Touching production code, so out of scope for this audit but straightforward.
tasks.why: Authentication gates every other feature and is the only feature area with zero test coverage. The account-switch case is a genuine untested risk: ContentView's @StateObject view models and the substitution cache are built once per app session and are not rebuilt on a user change.

tasks.title: Add a password reset flow
tasks.work: Add a 'Forgot password?' control to LoginView and an AuthViewModel.sendPasswordReset(email:) method wrapping Auth.auth().sendPasswordReset, with a confirmation state that does not disclose whether the address is registered.
tasks.acceptance: A reset email arrives for a registered address, and the UI response is identical for a registered and an unregistered address.
dependencies: P1 task 8, so the new method lands behind the testable abstraction
tasks.why: Account recovery is a baseline expectation for email/password sign-in. Today a forgotten password is unrecoverable from inside the app.

tasks.title: Replace the bundled recipe dataset with a real catalogue
tasks.work: Choose a source (a recipe API, or Firestore as the recipe store), implement RecipeRepository against it with response models, error mapping and caching, and inject it in ContentView.
tasks.acceptance: The recipe list is served from the remote source with loading and failure states, and feasibility still evaluates correctly against it.
tasks.effortAssumption: Dominated by the adapter and data modelling. The RecipeRepository protocol means no use case or view changes — injection in ContentView is one line.
tasks.why: Ten hard-coded recipes bound how useful feasibility matching can be: most real pantries will not match any of them. This is the biggest limitation on the product's core value proposition, independent of code quality.

tasks.title: Close the pantry loop: deduct ingredients after cooking
tasks.work: Add a ConsumeRecipeIngredientsUseCase with unit-aware subtraction, refusing to deduct where MeasurementUnit.convert returns nil (consistent with how the rest of the app fails closed), plus a 'Cooked this' action on RecipeDetailView.
tasks.acceptance: Marking a recipe cooked decrements the right pantry quantities, never below zero, and leaves unconvertible units untouched with an explanation.
tasks.effortAssumption: Follows the established use-case pattern and reuses existing conversion logic.
tasks.why: Without this, pantry quantities drift from reality the moment the user cooks anything, which degrades every feasibility verdict and every AI suggestion. It is the natural completion of the pantry/recipe loop the whole app is built around. Flagged as a recommendation because its presence in the Notion specification could not be confirmed.

tasks.title: Add UI journey tests and a shared scheme, then CI
tasks.work: Commit a shared FridgeFit.xcscheme under xcshareddata/xcschemes/ and resolve whether the uncommitted DEVELOPMENT_TEAM change belongs in version control. Add a UI test target with two or three high-value journeys. Add a GitHub Actions workflow running xcodebuild test on an iOS 26.1 simulator, injecting GoogleService-Info.plist from a repository secret.
tasks.acceptance: A clean clone plus the injected secrets builds and runs the full suite from the command line, and the workflow runs on every push.
dependencies: A decision on how CI receives the gitignored Firebase config
tasks.effortAssumption: Scheme and workflow are quick; the UI test target and journeys are most of the time. Assumes the secrets-injection approach is settled first.
tasks.why: With 240 tests and no automation, a regression is caught only when someone remembers to run the suite. The absence of integration tests is the structural reason so much of this audit reads 'needs verification'.

tasks.title: Resolve the Swift 6 concurrency warnings
tasks.work: Address the 11 'call to main actor-isolated X in a synchronous nonisolated context' warnings, then consider moving SWIFT_VERSION from 5.0 to 6.0.
tasks.acceptance: The build is warning-free, and the decision on Swift 6 language mode is recorded.
tasks.effortAssumption: Mostly annotation changes; some may need a type's isolation reconsidered.
tasks.why: These are warnings today only because SWIFT_VERSION is 5.0 while SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION is MainActor. Under Swift 6 language mode they become errors. ReceiptScannerViewModel's deinit comment documents a related runtime abort already encountered in this target, so this is not purely cosmetic.

tasks.title: Unify ingredient identity across scan, pantry and recipes
tasks.work: Carry canonicalName onto PantryItem and use it for duplicate detection and recipe ingredient matching, instead of discarding it at the pantry boundary.
tasks.acceptance: A hand-typed 'Bell Pepper' and a scanned 'Red Capsicum' are recognised as one ingredient, and a pantry 'Chicken' satisfies a recipe's 'Chicken Breast'. Existing Firestore documents without the field still decode.
dependencies: P0 task 3, so the schema change is covered by emulator tests
tasks.effortAssumption: Includes a Firestore schema addition that must be optional in the decoder, and a careful review of which merges become possible.
tasks.why: IngredientCanonicalizer is 297 well-tested lines that resolve 'CAPS RED', 'Red Capsicum' and 'Bell Pepper' to one identity — and that work is used only for scan-time dedupe, then thrown away. The pantry and recipe matcher both fall back to exact-after-normalisation name comparison. Note the risk: a wrong merge is harder for a user to notice than a missed one, which is why the canonicaliser's own descriptor list is deliberately conservative.

tasks.title: Decide the unit-conversion story
tasks.work: Either add volume ratios for cup/tbsp/tsp, or restrict the unit pickers to the units the app can reason about, or label the unconvertible units at the point of selection.
tasks.acceptance: A user cannot unknowingly create a pantry item in a unit that feasibility can never evaluate.
tasks.effortAssumption: Depends on the option chosen; restricting the pickers is the cheapest.
tasks.why: MeasurementUnit offers eight units but only four convert. The UI invites the user to pick cups, tbsp, tsp or pcs, and any pantry item in those units is permanently 'Check amount' against a recipe in grams. Failing closed is the right behaviour; the gap is the unit set offered.

tasks.title: Verify accessibility
tasks.work: Run Xcode's Accessibility Inspector audit on every screen, test with VoiceOver, and check the largest Dynamic Type sizes — particularly ReceiptItemReviewView, whose row packs a fixed 110-point quantity field and two pickers into one horizontal stack.
tasks.acceptance: The audit is clean, each screen is navigable with VoiceOver, and no layout clips at the largest accessibility text sizes.
tasks.effortAssumption: Verification plus likely small layout fixes in the receipt review row.
tasks.why: The accessibility work already present is deliberate and better than typical for a project this size — composed labels, hints, hidden decorative icons, colour always paired with a symbol and text. It is unverified rather than absent, so this is confirmation work.

tasks.title: Write setup documentation
tasks.work: Add a README covering the Firebase configuration step, the Secrets.xcconfig step, the iOS 26.1 and Apple Intelligence device requirements, and how to run the tests.
tasks.acceptance: Someone with a fresh clone can build, run and test the project from the README alone.
tasks.why: The repository has no README. Two required files are gitignored by design and two features are hardware-gated, so a fresh clone fails in several non-obvious ways with no written guidance.

tasks.title: Remaining deferred scope
tasks.work: Expiry tracking, pantry and recipe search/filter, an explicit offline policy, recipe imagery, favourites, acting on an AI suggestion, applying a substitution, profile editing, account management, app settings, email-format validation, email verification, localisation, and crash reporting.
tasks.acceptance: Per requirement; see the traceability matrix.
dependencies: Prioritisation against the Notion Feature List, which is the blocker on sequencing any of these
tasks.effortAssumption: Deliberately not estimated: without the specification there is no basis for deciding which of these are requirements and which are suggestions, and estimating them would imply a scope decision that is not the auditor's to make.
tasks.why: Grouped because their priority cannot be established from the code alone. Two are worth singling out: account deletion (CD-PROFILE-05) carries a privacy and in some jurisdictions a legal expectation, and would need a plan for the orphaned Firestore subcollection; and crash reporting (CD-INFRA-10) matters precisely because the Apple Intelligence paths this audit could not verify would fail invisibly after release.

topFiveDevelopmentTasks: Obtain the Notion Feature List and re-run the requirement mapping — nothing about overall completeness can be stated honestly until this is done.
Deploy the Firestore security rules and add cross-user denial tests.
Verify Firestore pantry CRUD against the Firebase Emulator Suite.
Configure OpenRouter credentials so Find Substitute works at all, and validate it live.
Build the dietary preferences profile, which is what makes the already-tested substitution restriction logic do anything.
topValidationActivities: One documented end-to-end receipt scan on Apple Intelligence-capable hardware, through to verified Firestore documents (CD-SCAN-10) — the project's largest unverified claim.
One documented Pantry Ideas generation on the same hardware, judging usefulness and latency from real model output rather than from the prompt (CD-AI-01).
Manual authentication verification: registration, sign-in, Google sign-in, relaunch persistence, sign-out, and the untested account-switch scenario (CD-AUTH-01 through CD-AUTH-05).
Confirmation that the live Firebase project enforces the committed rules rather than test-mode defaults (CD-PANTRY-07).
Live OpenRouter requests measuring latency, JSON compliance and whether the model respects the instruction never to assert pantry availability (CD-SUBST-02).
nextSteps.beforeDeclaringComplete: Three things block a credible completion claim, in order. First, the specification: 65 code-derived requirements are a provisional baseline, and a requirement nobody implemented leaves no code trace to find. Second, integration evidence: 240 passing unit tests cover domain logic thoroughly and cover the four production integrations not at all. Third, device evidence: the two Apple Intelligence features and the camera cannot run on a simulator, so the app's headline capability has not been observed working by this audit.

qualityFindings.title: Substitutions are non-functional in a fresh checkout
qualityFindings.detail: Secrets.xcconfig is absent, so OPENROUTER_API_KEY resolves empty, loadFromInfoPlist returns nil, and ContentView wires UnconfiguredSubstitutionService. Every Find Substitute tap fails with .notConfigured.

qualityFindings.title: Dietary restriction enforcement is built, tested and permanently inert
qualityFindings.detail: dietaryRestrictions defaults to [] and SubstitutionViewModel.findSubstitutes never passes it. A grep across the codebase finds it supplied non-empty only in test code.

qualityFindings.title: Camera usage description describes a removed feature
qualityFindings.detail: NSCameraUsageDescription still says the camera is used to photograph the inside of the fridge. The fridge-photo scanner was replaced by receipt scanning in commit b79ee34. CameraAccess.denied carries the same stale wording.

qualityFindings.title: Canonical ingredient identity is computed then discarded at the pantry boundary
qualityFindings.detail: IngredientCanonicalizer resolves 'CAPS RED', 'Red Capsicum' and 'Bell Pepper' to one identity, and ReceiptIngredientCandidate carries it, but PantryItem does not. Pantry duplicate detection and recipe matching both fall back to exact-after-normalisation display names.

qualityFindings.title: Eight selectable units, four convertible
qualityFindings.detail: cups, tbsp, tsp and pcs are offered in every unit picker but can never be compared to anything else, so such pantry items are permanently 'Check amount' against a recipe in grams.

qualityFindings.title: 17 Swift concurrency warnings (11 unique) in the test build
qualityFindings.detail: All of the form 'call to main actor-isolated X in a synchronous nonisolated context'. Warnings today because SWIFT_VERSION is 5.0 while SWIFT_DEFAULT_ACTOR_ISOLATION is MainActor; errors under Swift 6 language mode. ReceiptScannerViewModel's deinit comment documents a related runtime abort already hit in this target.

qualityFindings.title: Account switching within one session is untested
qualityFindings.detail: ContentView builds every view model and the SubstitutionCache once in init; they are not rebuilt on sign-out and sign-in. The Firestore repository re-reads the UID per call, so persistence follows the user, but in-memory lists and the cache may not.

qualityFindings.title: Multi-row pantry deletion spawns concurrent tasks
qualityFindings.detail: removeItems(at:) starts one unstructured Task per offset, each reloading the list on completion. The end state is correct because operations are id-scoped, but the intermediate list can flicker and the reloads are redundant.

qualityFindings.title: Updating an untouched quantity can write back a rounded value
qualityFindings.detail: UpdatePantryItemView seeds its field by splitting item.formattedQuantity, which MeasurementUnit.formatted has already rounded to one decimal place.

qualityFindings.title: Accepted scan drafts are matched by name rather than id
qualityFindings.detail: addSelectedToPantry removes drafts by comparing names against summary.addedNames. Two drafts with the same display name would both be removed when one was added. The id is available and would be exact.

qualityFindings.title: Mock and in-memory doubles ship in the production target
qualityFindings.detail: MockReceiptScanning, MockSubstitutionService, MockRecipeSuggestionService, InMemoryPantryRepository and InMemoryRecipeRepository live in FridgeFit/Data rather than the test target. This keeps them available to SwiftUI previews but includes them in the app binary.

qualityFindings.title: Machine-specific signing identity in an uncommitted pbxproj change
qualityFindings.detail: The working tree adds DEVELOPMENT_TEAM to both build configurations. A developer-specific team id in a shared project file breaks other developers' and CI builds.

strengths.title: Generative model output is never trusted with pantry state
strengths.detail: All three AI features follow the same pattern: model output enters as an untrusted Raw* type carrying no pantry claims, and a deterministic validator decides availability from the real pantry. ReceiptItemNormalizer discards any item whose echoed line was never sent — the hard stop on invented groceries. SubstitutionSuggestionValidator is the only type permitted to decide pantry existence, sufficiency and unit compatibility. SuggestRecipesFromPantryUseCase recomputes the available/missing split rather than asking for it. Each has a test asserting the adversarial case by name.

strengths.title: 'Not known' is modelled as a real answer rather than defaulted
strengths.detail: A receipt line with no quantity yields nil, not '1 pcs', and the UI says 'Quantity not detected'. An unconvertible unit pair yields quantityUnverified rather than a guessed comparison. An unrecognised Apple Intelligence unavailability reason fails closed. The removed confidence badge is documented as having measured nothing and given the user nothing to act on.

strengths.title: Tests assert documented invariants, not just code paths
strengths.detail: 240 tests, all passing, weighted toward the riskiest logic. Several assert properties rather than behaviour — that the interpreter only ever receives cleaned text, that a scan stores nothing on its own, that availability is checked before any OCR work, and that the prompt still forbids inventing products. Asserting prompt content is unusual and guards the instructions carrying the safety properties against accidental edits.

strengths.title: Privacy decisions are deliberate and documented
strengths.detail: ReceiptScanDiagnostics uses print behind #if DEBUG rather than Logger, with the reasoning stated: a receipt records what someone bought, where and when, and the unified log persists on device and is collectable in a sysdiagnose. SubstitutionRequest carries no ids and nothing about the Firebase user. The receipt photo never reaches the language model, and the scanner screen tells the user so.

strengths.title: Non-obvious decisions carry their reasoning in the source
strengths.detail: usesLanguageCorrection = false is explained by what it would break (correction rewrites CHKN toward a real word and the interpreter then faithfully reads the wrong product). The parser's weak-filter asymmetry is argued from which error the user can see. The nonisolated deinit on ReceiptScannerViewModel documents a specific runtime abort. This is why the audit could assess intent, not just behaviour.
